narrative.overview: The interface is a calm operational workspace shaped by AIA's motorsport identity. It uses disciplined white surfaces, charcoal structure and small, meaningful doses of AIA red so administrators and company leaders can understand status and take the next action quickly. Information density is deliberate: related facts stay together, repeated actions share one component, and workflow language remains human rather than technical.
keyCharacteristics: White working surfaces on a soft neutral field.
AIA red reserved for action, urgency and active navigation.
Compact line icons and concise, locale-specific copy.
Responsive layouts that simplify without hiding required information.

rules.name: The Red Means Something Rule
rules.body: Red marks a primary action, active location or item requiring attention; it is not general decoration.

rules.name: The One Locale Rule
rules.body: A screen shows Portuguese or English, never both versions of the same label at once.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: A normal card needs a border, not a shadow. Elevation communicates stacking or temporary focus.

dos: Do reuse the same component for the same interaction across roles and routes.
Do make the next operational action obvious and link notifications to the relevant workflow.
Do use icons from the established stroke vocabulary with accessible labels on controls.
Do validate desktop and mobile layouts whenever a global shell component changes.
donts: Don't expose database identifiers, hashes, enum values or immutable-version terminology to operators.
Don't duplicate Portuguese and English copy on the same selected-locale screen.
Don't add sidebar destinations for account or notifications; they belong in the global header.
Don't create one-off variants when an existing reusable pattern performs the same job.
